story.title: Duncan Sheik, Notable Singer and Broadway Composer, Passes Away at 56
story.summary: Duncan Sheik, known for his hit song 'Barely Breathing' and as the composer of the Tony Award-winning musical 'Spring Awakening,' has died at the age of 56. His family confirmed that he passed away due to organ failure. Sheik transitioned from pop music to musical theater, earning acclaim for his work on Broadway.

explore_lenses.label: What is confirmed about Sheik’s death?
explore_lenses.title: Death confirmed; medical details remain limited
explore_lenses.summary: Sheik’s death was publicly confirmed on September 18 after his family had said the day before that he was in critical but stable condition. Reporting identifies organ failure as the cause, but the family’s public announcement did not disclose medical specifics.

claims.text: A post on Sheik’s Instagram account said he died Thursday night; AP reported that he was 56.
Suzanne Sheik, his mother, told The New York Times that organ failure was the cause of death, according to AP and Fox News.
On September 16, a family statement said Sheik was receiving medical care and was in critical but stable condition, while asking that further medical details not be shared.

explore_lenses.label: Why was Sheik important beyond one hit?
explore_lenses.title: A pop success became a Broadway milestone
explore_lenses.summary: Sheik had an unusually durable crossover career: “Barely Breathing” made him a radio mainstay, while “Spring Awakening” made him a central figure in modern musical theater. His work with lyricist and book writer Steven Sater brought contemporary pop-rock into a show about adolescent repression and sexuality.

claims.text: “Barely Breathing” spent 55 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 and peaked at No. 16, according to AP.

The Tony Awards list Sheik as the 2007 winner for orchestrations for “Spring Awakening”; the show also won best musical and best original score, for which he wrote the music and Sater wrote the lyrics.

Sheik told the Associated Press in 2007 that the “Spring Awakening” team, largely Broadway outsiders, wanted to make a different kind of theater; later he described a goal of drawing people who would not normally attend musical theater.
AP reported that the original Broadway production ran for more than 860 performances beginning in 2006 and that it was revived on Broadway by Deaf West Theatre in 2015.

explore_lenses.label: What happens to the new “Spring Awakening”?
explore_lenses.title: An Off-Broadway production is still announced
explore_lenses.summary: Before Sheik’s death, Seaview announced a new Off-Broadway staging of “Spring Awakening” for fall 2026 at Studio Seaview. The announcement identifies a creative team, but the materials reviewed do not say whether the death will change the schedule or lead to a memorial component.

claims.text: Seaview’s June 10 announcement said the production would open Off-Broadway in fall 2026 at Studio Seaview, directed by Danya Taymor.
The announced team includes choreographer Celia Rowlson-Hall and music supervisor Or Matias.
AP likewise reported on September 18 that an Off-Broadway version was slated to open in fall 2026.

story_report.summary: Duncan Sheik, the singer-songwriter known for “Barely Breathing” and the composer of the Tony-winning musical “Spring Awakening,” died Thursday night at 56, according to a post on his Instagram account and Associated Press reporting. His family confirmed the death, and his mother, Suzanne Sheik, told The New York Times that organ failure was the cause. The loss ends a career that moved from a durable pop hit to acclaimed Broadway work, while a planned Off-Broadway “Spring Awakening” production had yet to announce any changes.

sections.heading: Duncan Sheik’s Pop and Broadway Career
sections.body: “Barely Breathing” spent 55 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 and reached No. 16, according to the Associated Press. Sheik later composed the music for “Spring Awakening,” with Steven Sater writing the lyrics; the show won the 2007 Tony Awards for best musical and best original score, while Sheik received the Tony for orchestrations. The original Broadway production began in 2006 and ran for more than 860 performances before Deaf West Theatre revived it on Broadway in 2015.

sections.heading: Spring Awakening’s Planned New York Return
sections.body: Before Sheik’s death, Seaview announced that “Spring Awakening” would return Off-Broadway in fall 2026 at Studio Seaview. The production was to be directed by Danya Taymor, with choreography by Celia Rowlson-Hall and music supervision by Or Matias. Associated Press also reported that an Off-Broadway version was slated for a fall 2026 opening.

unresolved.text: Public reporting does not establish the underlying illness, treatment timeline or a medical explanation beyond organ failure.
As of Sept. 18, 2026, no consulted announcement addressed whether Sheik’s death would alter the planned Off-Broadway production’s casting, dates, programming or tributes.

As a result, schools and universities suspended afternoon classes starting at 3 p.m. local time. The heavy rainfall raised concerns about further flooding and traffic disruptions in the capital.

related_stories.title: Fatal Shark Attack Claims Life of Swimmer Near Perth Beach
related_stories.summary: A man has died after being bitten by a shark while swimming at Sorrento beach in Perth, Western Australia. Emergency services responded to the incident around 10:30 AM on Friday, where witnesses reported a significant pool of blood in the water. This marks the fifth fatal shark attack in Australia this year.
